items.finding: The source reports that nitric acid and hydrochloric acid concentrations, ionic strength and temperature were varied to obtain a robust model.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests temperature should be treated as a variable in the measurement model; for the enquiry, it supports checking whether a temperature sensor at the probe is needed to capture local melt temperature.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The work concerns reactive liquid-liquid extraction, not hot polymer melt, and does not describe a probe-mounted temperature sensor.

citation.quote: The concentrations of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid as well as the ionic strength and temperature were varied to obtain a robust model.
citation.label: E01 ¶19

items.finding: The source notes that sample probe fouling was among the implementation limitations recognized for FTIR or FT-Raman.
items.how_it_applies: This supports treating probe fouling as a known implementation risk and considering cleaning or fouling detection in the probe design.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The context is biopharmaceutical Raman/FTIR history, not a hot polymer extrusion interface, so the fouling mechanism and cleaning needs may differ.

citation.quote: It was typical to see in those early reports that Raman was tested only after the implementation limitations of FTIR or FT-Raman, including sample probe fouling, high laser power, or incompatibility with aqueous systems, were recognized.
citation.label: E02 ¶8

items.finding: The source says fiber optic probes using a backscattered geometry with the focus slightly away from the optical window gave consistent and robust results across scales.
items.how_it_applies: This could inform probe geometry choices aimed at reducing window fouling or build-up effects, and suggests testing such a geometry at the process interface.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited results are not from hot polymer melt and do not establish build-up prevention, cleaning or detection performance.

citation.quote: Thus, fiber optic probes with a backscattered optical fiber geometry with a focus slightly away from the optical window have been shown to yield consistent and robust results across scales [45, 46].
citation.label: E02 ¶24

items.finding: The source states that an optical fiber system can be used to reduce the influence of heat development from the globar.
items.how_it_applies: This supports considering fiber coupling to separate the spectrometer heat source from the probe, but it does not give an achievable link length for a production extruder.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The statement comes from an in-line FTIR study of polysiloxane formation and does not report fiber length, mid-infrared transmission limits or extruder-scale installation.

citation.quote: In order to reduce the influence of heat development of the globar, an optical fiber system can be used.
citation.label: E03 ¶33
